chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who made it upon himself the fasting of a month in Al-Kufa, and a month in Al-Madina, and a month in Al-Makkah, due to an affliction he was tested with. So it was fulfilled that he fasted a month in Al-Kufa, and he entered Al-Madina and fasted eighteen days in it, and the camelier (or the one riding the camel) did not remain upon it (i.e., did not complete the fast while traveling). He (peace be upon him) said: 'He fasts what remains of it when he arrives at his city.'

key_terms.الْجَمَّال: The camelier or one riding a camel (implying travel)

ai.seo_question: How to fulfill a vow of fasting in multiple cities if one travels before completing them?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia juristic principle of flexibility in fulfilling conditional vows (nadhr) when travel interrupts the prescribed location, emphasizing that the obligation remains tied to the total duration rather than specific geography. It highlights the practical application of 'ease' (taysir) in Islamic law, allowing the vow-breaker to complete the remaining days in their home city after returning from travel, thereby preventing undue hardship.
